criteria_met: Identifies NLST CT volumes as the source of the generated projection images.
Describes parallel-beam projection generation, angular coverage, 5° sampling and subsequent tokenization.
Reports a patient-level partition for the CT-derived projection corpus.
criteria_missing: A pinned NLST release or data snapshot and operational image-level source-to-transformation lineage are not reported.
Projection intensity units, calibration and traceable normalization conversions are not specified.
Retention of acquisition and availability metadata is not documented.
assertions.rationale: The source describes more than a dataset name: it identifies the source-to-projection transformation and angular geometry. This is incomplete provenance, not an implemented full variable-level provenance contract.

criteria_met: Names the clinical-image source and reports training, validation and test CXR counts.
Identifies CycleGAN domain transformation before Xray2Xray feature extraction.
criteria_missing: The dataset release, image-level transformation lineage and CycleGAN checkpoint are not reported.
CycleGAN fitting data and its relationship to downstream test images are not specified.
Source-specific image calibration, units and acquisition/availability metadata retention are not documented.
assertions.rationale: Source identity and an actual transformation are described, but they do not establish complete provenance or test-set independence.

scope.time_horizon: Angular projection index over static CT-derived anatomy.

assertions.applicability_reason: The scoped transition traverses synthetically generated viewpoints of a static volume. It does not model recorded event or acquisition times, and there is no modeled temporal resolution at which native timestamps must be retained. Angular position is not a substitute for a recorded timestamp.
assertions.rationale: This disposition applies only to the angular synthesis task; it does not establish whether the original clinical datasets retain timestamps.

scope.time_horizon: Static-volume angular synthesis, not a clinical-time query.

assertions.applicability_reason: The reported synthesis query takes an initial projection and generates other angular views without a clinical information-release timeline. Collection-versus-release latency is therefore not part of this scoped task.
assertions.rationale: Availability of the initial input versus generated views remains important, but it is not an information-release timestamp mechanism.

scope.time_horizon: CVD risk endpoint and prediction horizon not sufficiently specified.

assertions.rationale: The CVD experiment reports labels and subject partitions but does not define decision-time availability, image-versus-outcome timing, release latency or a feature-availability audit. No future-information violation is established.

The described input comprises projection codes, direction tokens and class tokens. No measured/missing/invalid indicator or validity-mask treatment is reported. Autoregressive token ordering does not establish a missingness mask, and generating unobserved views is not itself missing-data handling.

scope.time_horizon: Angular sequence from static anatomy.

assertions.applicability_reason: The scoped model does not carry asynchronous clinical measurements forward in elapsed time. Its previous generated projection is a predecessor view, not a stale observation requiring per-variable time-since-measurement tracking.

scope.time_horizon: Equidistant 5° angular increments.

assertions.applicability_reason: No irregular elapsed-time prediction task is defined. The reported successor coordinate is a prescribed, uniformly sampled acquisition angle around static anatomy. Training epochs and autoregressive generation iterations are not physical time.
assertions.rationale: Uniform angular sampling does not establish failure to handle available unequal clinical intervals; no such intervals are used in this task.

The paper specifies a fixed angular projection-generation protocol and predicts image-code values conditional on direction and previous representation. It does not sufficiently describe a separate model of whether, when or why observations are obtained conditional on state. View-conditioned image generation is not automatically an informative-observation-process model.

scope.time_horizon: Prescribed angular sampling; no clinical observation clock is evaluated.

assertions.rationale: Neither the 5° projection spacing nor the 30° illustration is accompanied by a target-specific witness-preservation audit. No comparison of sampled values, update/validity patterns, native timing and external acquisition channels is reported. Projection similarity and tomographic reconstruction are different evaluations.

CycleGAN is used for image-domain adaptation, and an input resolution is specified. Neither establishes traceable mappings of source units, measurement definitions or terminology to a declared semantic target schema. No such harmonization procedure is reported.

criteria_met: Explicitly specifies a patient-level 70:10:20 training, validation and test partition for the CT-derived projection corpus.
criteria_missing: An explicit audit of training-only fitting for the VQ-GAN, codebook and preprocessing relative to the held-out patients is not supplied.
Exact patient identities, realized split counts and overlap verification are not reported.
No full feature-availability or contamination audit is reported.
assertions.rationale: Patient-level partitioning is a concrete leakage-control component. It does not by itself establish every required fitting and information-boundary safeguard.

criteria_met: Separately identifies training, validation and test subject sets for the downstream classifier.
Specifies validation-set rather than test-set learning-rate search.
criteria_missing: Overlap between the 1,000-volume CT pretraining corpus and the downstream NLST subject partitions is not reported.
Decision-time feature availability and timing relative to CVD labels are not sufficiently specified.
A complete preprocessing-fit and subject-overlap audit is not reported.
assertions.rationale: The stated partitions and validation-based tuning support a defined subset of preparation safeguards. They do not resolve pretraining contamination or outcome-timing questions, and no actual leakage is established.

criteria_met: Reports distinct training, validation and test CXR sets.
Describes learning-rate selection using validation data.
criteria_missing: Patient-level independence of the reported CXR partitions is not documented.
CycleGAN fitting data and exclusion of downstream test images from adaptation training are not specified.
No operational preprocessing-fit or overlap audit is reported.
assertions.rationale: Held-out clinical-image classification is reported, but adaptation and patient-independence safeguards are incomplete. This does not establish that the test set was actually reused.

No site-local training or query protocol, exchanged model artifacts, federation topology or communication mechanism is described. Multiple author affiliations and named datasets do not establish federation; the paper also does not explicitly document the incompatible identifiable-record pooling required for an absence assertion.

criteria_met: A trained VQ-GAN encoder maps projection images to quantized code-token sequences consumed by the transition model.
The token layout, codebook size and code dimension are reported.
Reconstruction results evaluate the operational autoencoding path.
assertions.rationale: The encoder is implemented and its representations are used in evaluated synthesis and classification pipelines. Reported fidelity results do not establish an unstated clinical acceptance threshold.

The authors train a VQ-GAN and subsequently freeze it, but no externally pretrained encoder checkpoint or transferred initialization is identified. Training the encoder in the first stage does not establish that initialization was from scratch. CheXFound, DINOv2 and iGPT comparisons are not foundation-encoder reuse by Xray2Xray.

scope.time_horizon: Next angular projection; not future patient time.

criteria_met: The transition target is a sequence of learned, quantized projection representations produced by the separately trained VQ-GAN encoder.
Equation (2) trains conditional prediction of those next-view representations using token negative log likelihood.
The transition-training objective does not require decoding predicted codes into pixels to compute its stated loss.
assertions.rationale: This satisfies the supplied operational criterion for predicting a target representation, specifically discrete learned latent codes rather than raw pixel tokens. It is not a claim that the method implements JEPA, a continuous embedding-matching loss or reconstruction-free training of the complete system. The VQ-GAN has a separate reconstruction objective, and no predictive-versus-reconstructive objective ablation is reported.

The paper specifies quantization, a learnable codebook, reconstruction training and subsequent encoder freezing, but does not explicitly describe an anti-collapse objective, code-utilization constraint, collapse-prevention argument or collapse assessment. Standard VQ-GAN mechanisms cannot be inherited from citations. The reported useful representations also do not establish that collapse was observed.

criteria_met: The first-stage discrete autoencoder is explicitly trained to reconstruct projection images.
A decoder maps the quantized representation back to image space.
Table 3 reports executed same-image reconstruction results for this autoencoder.
assertions.rationale: The reconstruction objective is implemented in the VQ-GAN stage. Its exact loss components and weights are not specified in this paper, and the cited VQ-GAN loss formulation is not imported. This assertion does not assign a pixel-reconstruction loss to the separately trained autoregressive transition.

assertions.applicability_reason: The model consumes X-ray projection images. Frontal and lateral views are views of the same modality; CT volumes generate training projections rather than forming a second inference modality. Concatenating two projection-derived trajectories therefore does not instantiate the listed multimodal-fusion feature.
assertions.rationale: This excludes multimodal fusion, not the documented two-view feature aggregation.

assertions.applicability_reason: The assessed implementation has no multimodal inference operation to condition on modality availability. Its single-view synthesis and same-modality two-view classification do not establish an applicable multimodal-fusion dependency.
assertions.rationale: Missing-view handling and image-quality robustness would remain separate reporting questions; they are not established by this applicability judgment.

scope.time_horizon: Recursive angular-view generation over the reported projection range, not clinical time.

criteria_met: A projection is represented by a defined discrete token sequence.
The preceding projection tokens and class-token conditioning enter the next-view prediction.
Predicted token sequences are recursively carried into subsequent predictions, with synthesis results reported for depth24.
assertions.rationale: The persistent evolving state is an acquisition-coordinate representation. This does not establish a physiological state or longitudinal patient dynamics.

Equation (1) defines a predictive distribution over next-projection tokens. The paper does not describe a posterior or filtering distribution over hidden anatomy conditioned on observation history, or give uncertainty semantics for such a belief. A generative token likelihood is not sufficient.

scope.time_horizon: Open-loop synthesis after the initial conditioning projection.

assertions.rationale: Scoped design absence: the specified inference algorithm recursively predicts from its own preceding outputs, and the illustrated synthesis explicitly receives no extra information. There is no distinct observation-conditioned correction operation within this executed rollout. This does not assert that a future extension could not add one.

scope.time_horizon: Reported inference trajectory after initialization.

assertions.rationale: The executed synthesis protocol uses an initial observed projection followed by generated projections without additional observations. Updating generated token state is not assimilation of newly arriving evidence. The absence assertion concerns this protocol, not an untested general interface capability.

Population pretraining, a frozen vision encoder, frozen downstream features and image-conditioned inference are described. No patient-specific parameter-fitting or weight-update rule using new individual measurements is reported. Frozen components alone are not treated as proof that every possible adaptation mechanism is absent.

criteria_met: The pretrained representation is used through frozen class-token features rather than a separately defined state model for each downstream task.
Separately trained readouts evaluate CVD risk classification and five-pathology classification.
assertions.rationale: This establishes representation reuse, not one unchanged clinical classifier or external validation of a fixed composed system. CheXpert additionally uses CycleGAN input-domain transformation.

Downstream classifiers probe representation utility, and Table 3 compares model depths and conditioning views. No matched omission, alteration or sufficiency-oriented probe isolates which state/history determinants are required for the prediction targets. General classification performance and a depth comparison are not promoted to state-sufficiency validation.

scope.time_horizon: Acquisition-view sequence initialized from an individual projection.

criteria_met: The individual's initial projection initializes the generated trajectory.
Each successor prediction explicitly depends on preceding projection state and rotation-action conditioning.
Recursive feedback transmits information from the initialized scene through later predictions.
assertions.rationale: This is scene/view-history conditioning, including generated predecessors. It is not evidence of multiple measured clinical visits, additional memory beyond supplied state, or demonstrated personalized predictive value.

The source reports individual-image conditioning, classification and reconstruction, but no matched input/history swap, withholding, population-prior or analogous control testing whether the correct individual's information adds value beyond a generic anatomical prior.

Conditional next-view generation and reconstruction of volumetric context are described, but no declared identity/anatomy-preservation memory, constraint or dedicated loss is specified. Visual resemblance and generic next-token supervision do not establish this mechanism.

The state consists of quantized projection codes and learned class tokens. Decoding images provides an inspectable output, but the paper does not map these state variables to interpretable anatomical entities or physiological quantities. No state-semantic inspection procedure is reported.

Equation (1) explicitly supplies the preceding projection and class token, with within-projection autoregression. The class token is said to summarize conditioning information, while an indexed K×D class-token embedding table is also described. Whether additional cross-projection history is retained beyond the supplied current state is insufficiently specified. Resolving class-token updates and any attention-context or cache persistence would settle this feature; recursive state feedback alone does not.

scope.time_horizon: Angular projection transitions.

criteria_met: A separate action token conditions next-projection prediction.
A two-category learned embedding represents clockwise and counter-clockwise rotation.
Action-conditioned projection synthesis is executed and evaluated.
assertions.rationale: The settable action changes modeled acquisition direction. It is neither a treatment variable nor evidence of scanner actuation or causal therapeutic effects.

criteria_met: Action categories have recoverable acquisition semantics: clockwise or counter-clockwise motion of the X-ray source.
The described static-volume projection setup identifies the modeled effect as a change in observed view.
criteria_missing: An implemented role/effect-channel typing scheme explicitly recording the acquisition/observation channel is not described.
No operational role/channel separation mechanism beyond the direction-category embedding is specified.
assertions.rationale: This is partial semantic coverage, not a claim that a full typed-action service exists. The missing criterion is explicit role/channel representation, not the absence of therapeutic or operational actions that this model does not need.

assertions.applicability_reason: The smaller synthesis configuration uses the same projection-image modality. Frontal and lateral conditioning are separately reported synthesis conditions, not two fused modalities. CT is the projection-generation source, not a second simultaneous inference input.

The reported depth12 synthesis configuration has no multimodal-fusion operation whose behavior depends on modality availability. Separate frontal- and lateral-seeded synthesis results do not constitute such an operation.

scope.time_horizon: Recursive acquisition-angle trajectory.

criteria_met: The common Xray2Xray method carries projection-token state into successor prediction.
The recursive synthesis procedure is evaluated for the 12-layer configuration in Table 3.
assertions.rationale: Depth12 has its own reported synthesis results. Depth24 metric values and the particular Figure 2 example are not transferred to this configuration.

The common method defines next-projection token probabilities, and Table 3 identifies depth12 synthesis performance. Neither specifies a posterior/filtering distribution over hidden anatomical state or its uncertainty semantics.

scope.time_horizon: Reported recursive synthesis after initialization.

assertions.rationale: Scoped design absence: the common inference algorithm used for the synthesis comparison recursively supplies predicted projection tokens to the next transition, with no observation-correction operation. Depth12 is evaluated as a smaller version of this synthesis architecture; no separate filtering algorithm is described.

scope.time_horizon: Open-loop generation from an initial frontal or lateral projection.

assertions.rationale: The specified synthesis protocol starts from an initial view and feeds back generated states, rather than ingesting arriving measured views. Table 3 evaluates this protocol for depth12. This is absence of assimilation in the executed protocol, not an assertion about all possible future uses.

Depth12 is reported as a pretrained projection-synthesis configuration. No individual fitting procedure or parameter update from new patient measurements is reported for it. Image-conditioned generation alone is not parameter adaptation.

Table 3 separately identifies the 154M depth12 synthesis model. The downstream evidence does not separately identify depth12 as feeding the CVD and CheXpert readouts; the CVD table instead reports a 391M Xray2Xray. Reuse demonstrated for the main configuration is not inherited by depth12.

The depth12/depth24 comparison changes model depth and parameter count, and frontal/lateral entries compare conditioning views. No depth12-specific state-determinant omission, history ablation or sufficiency-oriented probe is reported.

scope.time_horizon: Acquisition-view sequence initialized from an individual projection.

criteria_met: The common inference method initializes from the subject's projection.
Subsequent predictions explicitly depend on predecessor projection state and rotation-action conditioning.
assertions.rationale: Table 3 documents execution of the smaller model under frontal and lateral conditioning. This is scene-history dependence through recursive state, not evidence of extra memory or clinical longitudinal history.

Depth12 synthesis scores are reported, but no matched individual-input swap, withholding or population-prior control tests whether the correct person's anatomy materially determines its predictions beyond a generic prior.

The common next-projection objective and depth12 image-similarity results do not specify an identity/anatomical-consistency loss, constraint or dedicated memory mechanism. Generic conditional generation is not sufficient evidence for this feature.

No anatomical or physiological semantic mapping for depth12's code tokens or class-token coordinates is supplied. Its decoded projection outputs and PSNR/SSIM scores do not establish interpretable state variables.

The common transition equation supplies the preceding projection and a class token, but does not resolve whether that token or an attention cache retains additional cross-projection history. No depth12-specific memory specification resolves the ambiguity. Recursive projection feedback and Transformer architecture alone do not establish memory beyond the supplied state.

scope.time_horizon: Angular projection transitions.

criteria_met: The common transition architecture takes a separately encoded rotation-direction action.
Depth12 is evaluated for projection synthesis using that architecture.
assertions.rationale: This supports specified-action acquisition prediction for depth12. It does not transfer the particular Figure 2 matched-alternative example or depth24 numerical results to the smaller model.

criteria_met: The shared action vocabulary has explicit clockwise/counter-clockwise acquisition-motion meaning.
Its modeled effect is a change in projection viewpoint around static anatomy.
criteria_missing: An operational role/effect-channel typing scheme beyond rotation-direction categories is not reported.
The observation-channel interpretation is recoverable from the physical setup but is not explicitly represented as typed action metadata.
assertions.rationale: The same semantic limitation applies to the smaller architecture. Unused therapeutic or operational action categories are not required, and no real acquisition-device execution is inferred.

scope.time_horizon: Angular projection index; 5° increments within [−90°,90°].

assertions.rationale: The query has two specified rotation directions, an angular increment in degrees, and a reference geometry with the anterior-posterior frontal projection at 0°. These semantics suffice to interpret the synthetic next-view query. Drug attributes, physical movement duration and scanner actuation parameters are not required for this indexed geometric query and are not asserted.

scope.time_horizon: Direction-conditioned actions indexed by successive angular projection steps.

assertions.rationale: Equation (1) associates action a_(t−1) with the successor projection r_t, and the implemented recursive sequence has a declared 5° angular cadence. This establishes an index-based acquisition-action sequence, not a physical-time movement schedule, treatment schedule or demonstrated ability to execute arbitrary direction-switching schedules.

assertions.applicability_reason: The scoped action is a single rotation-direction category for generating views around a static CT-derived anatomy. No joint treatment components or linked clinical settings are represented or edited, so coherent treatment-bundle update semantics do not apply.

assertions.rationale: The paper specifies two direction categories and the generated/evaluated angular range, but does not describe a context-dependent candidate-action filter, workspace enforcement rule or contraindication mechanism. Dataset coverage and a finite rollout range alone do not establish an implemented constraint guard.

Semantic grounding is established within the synthetic acquisition environment: the two action embeddings explicitly correspond to clockwise and counter-clockwise X-ray-source rotation in a defined angular projection geometry. They are not uninterpreted latent edits. This assessment does not establish calibrated scanner commands, robot control, radiation delivery or an executable clinical acquisition interface.

Training-view coverage and synthesis within the angular grid are reported, but no context-conditioned action-support criterion, support-based query restriction or extrapolation test is described. Tomographic angular coverage is not itself an evaluated action-support mechanism.

scope.population: The illustrated CT-derived thoracic scene in Figure 2.
scope.time_horizon: Same-origin clockwise and counter-clockwise angular branches displayed from a common 0° input.

assertions.rationale: The Figure 2 caption and supplied image-review transcription describe predictions in both specified rotation directions from the same frontal input, with per-view PSNR. This supports the existing annotation's narrow functional comparison interpretation, not an aggregate matched-regime experiment, action ranking, clinical treatment counterfactual or causal identification. The depth24 assignment follows the current annotation; Figure 2 does not explicitly label Transformer depth, so that configuration attribution remains a review limitation.

assertions.applicability_reason: The scoped actions generate synthetic projections offline and do not deliver radiation, move clinical hardware or intervene on a person. Physical/clinical reversibility and residual harm of executed actions therefore do not apply to this demonstrated environment. This does not establish safety for later clinical use.

scope.time_horizon: Successive acquisition-angle states within [−90°,90°], not elapsed patient time.

assertions.rationale: The carried projection tokens and class-token conditioning generate successor-view tokens, which are recursively reused and decoded for evaluated synthesis. The transition coordinate is acquisition angle around static anatomy. Neither training epochs nor angular steps represent disease-time evolution.

The Transformer transition itself is trained by next-projection negative log likelihood, with an executed training procedure and depth24 synthesis results. This satisfies the learned-transition branch of the feature; it does not assert a mechanistic–learned hybrid transition merely because the feature ID contains 'hybrid'.

scope.time_horizon: Recursive successor-view prediction under specified rotation-direction inputs.

assertions.rationale: The conditional transition explicitly consumes a settable action token, the embedding vocabulary specifies the two rotation directions, and action-conditioned projection synthesis is evaluated. The actions change modeled viewpoint, not physiology, and conditioning does not establish clinical causal effects.

criteria_met: Equation (1) specifies an autoregressive conditional probability distribution over the next projection's discrete tokens.
The transition distribution is fitted using negative log likelihood, and projection generation is executed.
criteria_missing: The inference token-selection or sampling procedure is not reported.
Non-degenerate conditional randomness used in executed next-state transitions is not established; greedy or other deterministic decoding is not excluded.
assertions.rationale: A fitted probabilistic transition formulation is supported, but stochastic execution is not fully documented. Table 3's undefined ± quantities do not demonstrate repeated stochastic futures, transition-noise semantics, uncertainty decomposition or calibration.

Tomographic geometry motivates the training projections, but the paper does not report a conservation law, anatomical constraint, projection-consistency equation or mechanistic regularizer operating on transition/representation learning. Filtered back projection is a downstream reconstruction operation, not evidence by itself of a mechanistic prior constraining the learned transition.

The reported state-advancing component is a learned Transformer. No mechanistic transition term, learned physical closure or fitted mechanistic state update is described. The separately documented neural-synthesis-to-filtered-back-projection reconstruction pipeline is retained as a composition fact, but is not promoted to a mechanistic–learned dynamics assertion about this transition model.

Depth12 and depth24 are reported architecture-size comparisons. The paper does not document exchanging them under a semantic state/action/time/output contract or integration-testing backend replacement. The VQ-GAN encoder/decoder and downstream reconstruction algorithm are different responsibilities, not additional interchangeable transition backends.

scope.population: Static thoracic anatomy represented through angular projections.

assertions.rationale: No distinct physical, spatial or temporal world levels with explicit cross-scale state exchange are reported. Two-dimensional projections, latent tokens and reconstructed volumetric context are representation/view transformations; their existence alone does not establish coupled multiscale dynamics. Separate NLST and CheXpert downstream tasks also do not establish such coupling.

scope.time_horizon: Angular projection index; shared synthesis setup with 5° projection spacing.

assertions.rationale: Depth12 is evaluated as a smaller Xray2Xray synthesis configuration under the shared direction-conditioned projection protocol. The action categories and angular geometry are sufficiently defined for this synthetic query. Depth24 performance values and an executable scanner interface are not inherited.

scope.time_horizon: Shared index-based angular synthesis sequence.

assertions.rationale: The shared method places direction actions at successive projection indices, with declared angular cadence, and Table 3 evaluates depth12 in that synthesis task. This is an acquisition-index schedule, not elapsed clinical time or a tested arbitrary action-switching policy.

assertions.applicability_reason: The depth12 configuration uses the same single rotation-direction action vocabulary. There are no linked treatment components or jointly updated clinical settings requiring treatment-bundle semantics.

assertions.rationale: Neither the shared method nor the depth12 results specify an action-filtering or workspace-enforcement mechanism. The training/evaluation angle range does not independently establish an implemented constraint on candidate queries.

The shared action vocabulary used by the depth12 configuration has explicit synthetic acquisition semantics: clockwise or counter-clockwise source rotation in a specified angular geometry. This establishes semantic grounding for the offline simulator query only, not hardware calibration, clinical command execution or validated latent-to-actuator alignment.

During inference, Xray2Xray re-

sequence of class tokens that encode 3D spatial representations for downstream

We trained Xray2Xray using 1,000 CT volumes from the National Lung Screen-
ing Trial (NLST) dataset. To generate X-ray projections, we first positioned the
X-ray source at 0 ◦ to obtain an anterior-posterior frontal projection, and then
rotated it counter-clockwise to −90◦ and clockwise to 90 ◦ to collect the remain-
ing views. With a parallel beam, the projections spanning [ −90, 90] satisfy the
requirements for tomographic reconstruction. The X-ray source was rotated in
equidistant steps of 5 ◦, resulting in 37 X-ray projections per CT volume. We
partitioned the dataset at patient level into training, validation, and test sets
with a 70:10:20 ratio.
For downstream adaptation, we applied Xray2Xray to two tasks: cardiovas-
cular disease (CVD) risk estimation on the NLST dataset and disease diagnosis
on the CheXpert dataset. For CVD risk estimation, we used labels annotated
by Chao et al. [1] with 7,268 subjects for training, 1,042 subjects for validation,
and 2,085 subjects for test. For disease diagnosis, we used labels provided by
CheXpert [9], containing 191,027, 202, and 518 CXRs for training, validation,
and test, respectively.

We trained VQ-GAN to tokenize X-ray projections from −90◦ to 90 ◦, using
a codebook size of 1024, a code dimension of 256, and an input resolution of
224. We trained VQ-GAN for 100 epochs using the Adam optimizer with a
learning rate of 4.5e-6 and a batch size of 12. We trained an autoregressive
Transformer on top of the VQ-GAN encoder with a latent output of 14 × 14
tokens. We set the default embedding dimension to D = 1024 for Transformer.
